finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id deletes any project regardless of ownership. The authorized() result is discarded, so a non-owner non-admin can delete another user's project.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled path parameter req.params.id (plus any authenticated session that reaches this router, as req.user).
finding.sink: req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at api.js:19, a destructive write on a protected resource.

trace.note: Route handler for DELETE /projects/:id; no auth or ownership check in the route itself.
project = req.store.projects.get(req.params.id): fetched by client-supplied id with no owner scope.
authorized(req.user, project) is called as a bare statement. It returns a boolean that is never read, so a false result (non-owner, non-admin) does not stop execution. It does not throw either.
req.store.projects.delete(project.id) runs unconditionally for any caller.
authorize() (throws) exists, but it is not used on this route. authorized() (lines 12-14) returns a boolean and is the helper called here.

finding.guards_checked: (1) authorized() at line 18: its boolean return is discarded, so it does not gate the delete. (2) authorize() at line 25 is the throwing variant and is correctly used on the PUT route, but not on DELETE. (3) Ownership fields: resource.ownerId === user.id || user.isAdmin === true is the intended predicate, and it is correct; the bug is only in how its result is used. (4) Router-level or app-level auth middleware is not in the scanned code (only api.js is present), so the precondition is that the caller is authenticated, which is assumed rather than verified. (5) Decoy check: case 27 and the 'checked object A, acted on object B' pattern (case 05) do not apply, because the check and the delete both use the same project object. Missing project: if get() returns undefined, line 18 throws a TypeError (500) before any delete, so that is not a bypass.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:18 is called as a bare statement, so its boolean return (defined at api.js:12-14) is discarded and does not gate the delete at api.js:19. authorize() (api.js:4-10, throwing variant) exists but is not used on the DELETE route; it is only used on the PUT route at api.js:25. No router- or app-level auth middleware is present (Glob shows api.js is the only file).
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:16-20 calls authorized() at line 18 without testing its result, so req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at line 19 runs for any caller who reaches the route, including non-owners. The attacker only needs to be an authenticated low-privilege user, since the only auth precondition is an assumed req.user, and no effective control blocks the delete.
